verdicts.evidence: baseline:3262 master_wine_id NOT NULL on restaurant_inventory; inventory_lots.master_wine_id NOT NULL and inventory_transactions.wine_id NOT NULL; qty/quantity_change/stock_live are integer. But migration 20260903171000:167-176 in the same tree DROPs those NOT NULLs, so 'every row needs a wine' is only true of the baseline. Open wine volume is already integer ml (inventory_lots.open_bottle_ml). @IsInt is 10 decorators in inventory.dto.ts and 3 in inventory-ledger.dto.ts (not 15 in one place), and most are bottle size, glasses, vintage, not stock quantity.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Baseline schema requires a wine link on the stock row, lot and ledger movement, and counts are integer; the unapplied-or-gated migration would relax the links; open bottles are already integer ml.

verdicts.evidence: photo-count.service.ts:14-22 prompt: one named wine, 'intact, visibly full-or-partial bottles', suggestedQty integer; :93 passes only the wine name; inventory.service.ts:660-663 falls back to 'this wine'. wholeNumber() in InventorySheets.tsx:43-47 rejects tenths. So single item, integer, no shelf recognition, no level: true. 'Whole bottles' is slightly off: partial bottles are counted as one each, not excluded.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Photo count is one item, one wine name, an integer that counts partial bottles as bottles; no level, no tenths, no multi-item shelf.

verdicts.evidence: detectMediaType (photo-count.service.ts:132-139) returns image/jpeg for anything not jpg/png/webp prefix, so HEIC and PDF (accepted by SCAN_ACCEPT, uploadAccept.ts:21-24, and used at InventorySheets.tsx:197) are mislabelled; client does readAsDataURL of the raw file with no resize (:145-157); service stores no image (recordPhotoCountSuggestion records the suggestion, inventory.service.ts:665-687). Caveat: iOS pickers often transcode HEIC to JPEG before upload, so HEIC mislabel is less likely in practice than PDF.

InventorySheets.tsx:163 prints '(${estimate.confidence} confidence)' where confidence is the model's own low/medium/high word (photo-count.service.ts:19); legacy SpotCountPanel.tsx:167 does the same. It is a word, not a number, so ADR 0104's number ban is not literally breached, but it is still a self-graded confidence shown to people.

OD-230 (OPEN-DECISIONS.md:319) asks about input modes (barcode, level tap, voice), not F1 period, F2 shelf-by-shelf post or F4 phone width, so it is weak evidence for those. True part: apps/mobile has cellar, supply, receive/[orderId] screens and receivingCountBasis.ts but no stock-count screen; web count is single-item (InventorySheets.tsx:171-216).
verdicts.corrected_claim: No phone stock-count session exists on mobile or web; OD-230 only covers input mode, the period/shelf-post/phone-width answers have no cited record in this evidence.

verdicts.evidence: fetchLotRollup/fetchLocationBreakdown destructure only {data} and drop error (inventory.service.ts:184,204); try/catch only catches thrown errors. On failure openMl becomes 0 (:163) and locations [] (:173). But wac and costProvenance become undefined, not zero/estimated (:154-159), and the analytics read does have an analyticsReadable flag on the web side, so only open ml and locations pose as health.

verdicts.evidence: After a single count, inventory.service.ts:595-606 refetches the row plus fetchLotRollup(restaurantId) and fetchLocationBreakdown(restaurantId), both whole-house (:178-189, :198-208), to return one item.

useRowDetail (useInventoryNextData.ts:823-835) fetches the ledger default 50 and keeps 3 (PAPERWORK_LINES=3), then documents per order: the waterfall is purchases then docs only. The record read runs five books in Promise.all (beverages.service.ts:781-787), reads the whole current menu (readCurrentMenuLines) and pages house_till_names (:1063-1068). All on the open gesture, not page load.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Row open does an over-fetch of 50 ledger rows to keep 3 then per-order doc reads, plus a parallel whole-menu and till-name read; none on page load.
